text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed clients seeing 200 but model changed due to routing fallback yesterday. Is that expected?
charlie: yeah saw it in traces. The routing layer swapped to gpt-small-128q when dedicated pool maxed. We returned 200 with a small body field 'served_variant'.
liam: we probably shouldn't make the model swap an invisible success signal. Clients need a deterministic way to detect downgraded quality. Maybe add a header like X-Rw-Fallback.
sophia: +1. Also telemetry needs an explicit tag so console charts can separate baseline vs fallback traffic.
maya: what about returning different HTTP status? my take: it's still a successful inference so 200 is fine; surface advisory header and a machine-readable code.
charlie: agreed. Options we discussed: 1) 200 + advisory header, 2) 200 + body field, 3) non-standard status (no). Let's avoid non-standard codes.
liam: SDKs should expose this as a warning event so apps can opt into alerts or fallback to local policy.
sophia: propose RFC: add header X-Rw-Fallback: variant=gpt-small-128q;severity=degraded;code=rw.routing.fallback.variant and a telemetry event routing.fallback.
maya: also think about quota signals — if fallback happened because reserved capacity hit its quota, include quota hint header.
charlie: +1 to a compact header set: fallback header and quota-hint header. Keep body minimal to avoid breaking consumers.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout v2.1 will add the fallback headers to the routing proxy starting 2026-02-12 03:00 UTC.
jordan: question: do we mark this as an "error" in logs or as an informational routing note? Product teams will want to see trends.
liam: treat it as a distinct telemetry event level=info but severity=degraded for quality monitoring. Console should be able to pivot on that field.
sophia: also, we need an explanation string for the console and i18n copy: "Requests were routed to a lower-capacity model due to capacity or quota constraints" — tooltip text.
maya: can we also expose remaining quota so customers can self-diagnose? X-Rw-Quota-Hint: tier=dedicated;remaining=0 seems useful.
charlie: agreed, but sanitize exact numbers for privacy; provide tier + approximate remaining (0, low, ok).
sophia: I'll draft the header schema and console card. PR incoming.
maya: thanks — please paste a quick example header snippet here so we can review. :pray:
sophia: snippet:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Rw-Fallback: variant=gpt-small-128q;severity=degraded;code=rw.routing.fallback.variant
X-Rw-Quota-Hint: tier=dedicated;remaining=0
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"req_abc","served_variant":"gpt-small-128q","result":"..."}
```
liam: looks good. Telemetry event should include {model_from,model_to,reason,request_id,timestamp}.
maya: can we rate-limit customer-visible alerts? maybe only surface a console alert if >5% of requests in a minute are fallback.
charlie: that threshold sounds reasonable. We'll add an internal default and allow customers to change it.
sophia: added to the RFC checklist: header schema, telemetry schema, SDK warning hooks, console tooltip + alerting threshold, docs.
jordan: pinging @product for final sign-off on header exposure and default alert thresholds.
maya: great, thanks all. I think this will make fallback behavior much more actionable for customers. :thumbsup:
